title: Disguised Face Emoji 🥸 Meaning: Incognito, But Obvious
description: 🥸 wears novelty glasses, a fake nose and a mustache. It means going undercover, pretending to be someone else or sneaking around, nearly always as a joke.
summary: The 🥸 disguised face means incognito in the least convincing way possible. People use it for sneaking around, pretending to be someone they are not, lurking on a profile or acting innocent after being caught. It can also poke fun at a person who is being fake or posing as an expert.
meaning: The glasses, plastic nose and bushy mustache are a classic joke-shop disguise, the kind associated with old comedy acts and known for fooling nobody. That is the heart of the emoji. 🥸 does not mean a real secret identity; it means a disguise so thin that everyone can see through it, and the sender knows it.

A common use is playful sneaking. Checking an ex's profile, watching a group chat without replying, slipping out of a party early, visiting a store you said you would stop spending money at: all of these get 🥸. It often comes with a pretend-innocent line such as nobody saw me or just passing through.

It also works for pretending to be something. Someone starting a new job with no idea what they are doing might send 🥸 to mean blending in. A person wearing a suit for once, or commenting in a field they know little about, uses it to admit they are in costume. Turned on others, it calls them a poser or a fraud.

Because the face looks like a middle-aged man with thick glasses, people use it for dad jokes and for mock-serious statements too, as if a stuffy expert were speaking. That reading overlaps with the nerd face, though 🥸 is about putting on an act rather than being a know-it-all, and it usually mocks the speaker more than the listener.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends send it when they are up to something harmless and want you to know. Me walking past your desk to steal a snack 🥸 is typical. It also softens a confession by turning it into a bit, and it answers who did this when the culprit is obvious.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It labels lurking, burner accounts and showing up where you are not expected. Fans use it when they slip into another fandom's comment section. It is popular in memes about pretending to understand a conversation or acting like a functioning adult.

contexts.label: About fake behavior
contexts.body: Replying 🥸 to someone's post can accuse them of being inauthentic: a brand pretending to be relatable, a new account that sounds a lot like a banned one, a friend acting as if they did not start the drama. The tone is teasing, but the point is that the mask is not working.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: In casual team chat it is a self-deprecating way to describe impostor feelings, such as joining a meeting far above your pay grade. It reads as humor. Using it about a colleague suggests they are faking competence, so keep it pointed at yourself.

examples.text: Me viewing your story from my other account 🥸
examples.meaning: Joking about watching someone's content in secret.

examples.text: First day as a manager, nobody tell them I have no idea what I'm doing 🥸
examples.meaning: Admitting to feeling like an impostor.
The sender did, and is pretending to be innocent.

examples.text: Showing up to the gym in January like I've always been here 🥸
examples.meaning: Trying to blend in somewhere new.
Mocking themselves or someone else for an obvious attempt to fit in.

examples.text: New account, same opinions 🥸 we see you
examples.meaning: Calling out someone whose cover is transparent.

combos.meaning: Lurking and watching while pretending not to be there.
Playing detective or going undercover to find something out.
Keep my secret; I was never here.
Dressing or acting the part of a professional without feeling like one.

confusedWith.difference: 🤓 has glasses and a toothy grin and stands for nerdiness or a know-it-all tone. 🥸 adds a fake nose and mustache and is about disguise and pretending. One is being smart; the other is faking it.
🧐 inspects something closely and looks genuinely skeptical or curious. 🥸 is the one being looked at, hoping not to be recognized. Detective versus suspect is a fair summary.
😎 hides its eyes behind shades and means cool and confident. 🥸 hides its whole identity, badly, and means sneaky or fake. Neither is serious, but only one thinks it looks good.

avoid: Do not use it to joke about actually deceiving someone who would be hurt by the lie.
Avoid calling a person fake with it in public unless you are prepared for an argument.
Skip it in messages about real fraud, scams or identity theft, where it trivializes the problem.
design: A yellow face wearing thick black-rimmed glasses attached to a large false nose, with heavy eyebrows and a bushy mustache. It depicts the novelty disguise sold in joke shops. Platforms draw it very similarly; the main variation is the mustache and eyebrow color, usually black or dark brown, and whether a mouth is visible beneath.

faqs.a: That the sender is being sneaky, pretending or hiding in plain sight, and finds it funny. It nearly always has a comic tone. The disguise is supposed to be bad, so the emoji admits to the very thing it claims to conceal.

faqs.q: What does 🥸 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Usually a joke about lurking or acting casual, such as looking at your profile and pretending they did not. It has no fixed romantic meaning, though admitting to checking your page can be a light form of flirting.

Not seriously. It can tease a person for being fake or putting on an act, and it can confess to a small fib. For real dishonesty people use the lying face 🤥 or say so directly. 🥸 keeps things in the realm of humor.

faqs.q: When was the disguised face emoji added?
faqs.a: It was approved in Unicode 13.0 in 2020, along with the smiling face with tear, the pinched fingers gesture and the people hugging emoji. It is available on all current phones and computers.
